programme_detail_official.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme awards a scholarship to exceptional international students commencing a coursework degree at the University of Sydney. Five award amounts are offered on the basis of ranking against the selection criteria: AUD 60,000 and AUD 40,000 for one year, and AUD 20,000, AUD 10,000 and AUD 5,000 for one semester. No application is required, because eligibility is determined by receiving an unconditional offer of admission in a qualifying offer round by the published close date. Recipients must maintain a minimum semester average mark of 65 and cannot accept another University of Sydney scholarship valued above AUD 20,000 per annum.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply for a CRICOS-registered onshore bachelor's or coursework master's degree, since the scheme is limited to onshore coursework awards
Target an offer round deliberately: the 5 October 2026 and 16 November 2026 Round 2 and Round 3 closes for Semester 1, 2027 are the near-term windows
Make sure you accept the unconditional offer by the deadline attached to that offer round, because acceptance after the deadline forfeits consideration
Check you are not already holding an Australian Government scholarship, which makes you ineligible
Accept that the award is capped at AUD 40,000 if you also hold a Sydney International Student Award
Plan to maintain a minimum semester average mark of 65 and clear any outstanding fees, or the second instalment is withheld
common_rejection_risks: Missing the acceptance deadline that matches the offer round, which is separate from the round close date
Holding or accepting an Australian Government scholarship
Holding another University of Sydney scholarship worth more than AUD 20,000 per annum, which terminates the award
Falling below a semester average mark of 65 or leaving fees outstanding between instalments
Applying to a degree that is not CRICOS registered or not delivered onshore
Expecting a renewable award: it is awarded only once, on commencement, and is not renewable
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, which this award does not state that it covers
Living costs and accommodation beyond the scholarship amount
Travel costs to and from Australia
The gap between the scholarship received and the full cost of the degree, which is substantial for most award tiers

Records needed to demonstrate a semester average mark of 65 once enrolled

alerts.message: You must accept your unconditional offer by the deadline linked to your scholarship offer round, which is earlier than the general admissions deadline.

If you also hold a Sydney International Student Award your VCIS is capped at AUD 40,000, and from 2026 intakes the termination threshold for other University of Sydney scholarships rose to AUD 20,000 per annum.
The University states the scholarship will be offered subject to the availability of funds, so an award is not guaranteed even if you are eligible.

submission_workflow: Choose your offer round and note both its close date and the acceptance deadline attached to it
Apply for an eligible CRICOS-registered onshore coursework degree through the University of Sydney admissions process
Receive and accept the unconditional offer by the deadline linked to that round
Wait for the automatic scholarship assessment; no separate submission is made
If awarded, note which tier you received and the instalment schedule
Maintain a semester average mark of 65 and keep fees clear so the second instalment is released

programme_detail_official.description: The Farrand Scholarship in Agricultural Science is a University of Sydney undergraduate award, established in 2023 from a donation by the Estate of Annie Farrand, for exceptional international students from diverse priority markets. It is valued at AUD 20,000 per annum for up to three years and is tenable only by students enrolled full-time in the Bachelor of Agricultural Science or Bachelor of Agricultural Science (Honours) in the Faculty of Science. No application is required, because all eligible students who have secured an unconditional offer are automatically considered, and the award is made on academic merit as assessed from the admission application and on the nomination of the Dean of the Faculty of Science.

programme_detail_official.description: The ANU Chancellor's International Scholarship is a tuition fee reduction for overseas students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate degree, or a graduate certificate, at the Australian National University. Awards are distributed into 9 citizenship-based categories with at least one open worldwide, and applicants are automatically assessed first for the highest-value award for which they are eligible. The reduction is 25% of tuition fees, or 25% or 50% in the South East Asia and Europe, Central and South Americas categories, applied for the duration of the degree, with guaranteed first-year accommodation available. As at 2026-10-04 the official page states that the scholarship is currently unavailable and the application period is closed.

programme_detail_official.coverage: Partial tuition only: 25% of tuition fees, or 25% or 50% in two categories, for the duration of the degree, plus guaranteed accommodation for the first year of study. No stipend, travel support or separately itemised living-cost component is published.

programme_detail_official.description: The Global Excellence Scholarship is an annual tuition fee discount awarded automatically by the University of Western Australia to high-achieving international students from any country who take an eligible 2027 undergraduate or postgraduate course. The discount is 10 or 20 per cent of tuition fees for the normal full-time duration of the course, and its value is set by the applicant's equivalent ATAR for undergraduate study or UWA weighted average mark for postgraduate study. No separate scholarship application is required, because UWA Admissions assesses eligibility automatically once final transcripts are received. The scholarship is in place for the 2027 to 2029 intakes and cannot be held alongside any other UWA tuition fee reduction, scholarship or award.

programme_detail_official.coverage: Tuition fees only, at 10 or 20 per cent for the normal full-time duration of the course. No accommodation, living-cost, travel or stipend component is published.
